notice: Candidate internal policies and synthetic payloads only. A listed case proves its stated boundary, not full metric acceptance, source completeness or a public launch gate.

cases.name: PR creation credits its author and original clock, not the delivery sender
cases.inclusion: A draft PR still contributes one creation unit to its author.
cases.exclusion: Missing creation time and a merger-role selection cannot supply author credit.

cases.name: first readiness survives toggles without inventing current-state history
cases.inclusion: Two witnessed readiness observations conserve the first-ready author unit.
cases.exclusion: A later toggle outside the first-ready window, an unproven toggle and a current snapshot do not contribute.

cases.name: merged participation uses the PR author and merge clock
cases.inclusion: One merged object contributes one author unit across repeated observations.
cases.exclusion: Closed-unmerged, missing merged_at, merger-role selection and out-of-window merges do not contribute.

cases.name: verified coauthors stay separate from primary authors and pending work
cases.inclusion: An independently linked coauthor receives one merged participation unit even with repeated links.
cases.exclusion: Primary-author overlap, an empty verification receipt and an unmerged PR do not become coauthor delivery.

cases.name: merged_by remains distinct from the author, sender and automation lens
cases.inclusion: The merger receives one operation; a Bot merger is visible only in the automation selection.
cases.exclusion: The sender cannot fill missing merged_by, and a Bot merger cannot receive user-lens credit.

cases.name: the decided-PR denominator excludes pending PRs and duplicate observations
cases.inclusion: One merged and one closed-unmerged decision produce numerator1, denominator2 and share0.5.
cases.exclusion: A pending PR stays separate; replay does not enlarge the denominator, and ranking or creation-time ratios are rejected.

cases.name: decisions require exact selected history and an empty denominator is unavailable
cases.inclusion: A pending object remains visible as pending1 with numerator0 and denominator0.
cases.exclusion: Absent, unverified, different-as-of or contradictory decision histories cannot contribute a decided fact; no decided sample is null, not0%.

cases.name: submitted reviewer participation is independent of approval preference
cases.inclusion: COMMENTED, APPROVED and CHANGES_REQUESTED observations from one reviewer yield one reviewer-PR participation.
cases.exclusion: PR self-review, Bot review, pending draft review and author-role selection do not contribute.

cases.name: head-specific rounds conserve repeat submissions without favoring approval
cases.inclusion: Two reviews on one head and one on a second head yield two rounds but one reviewed PR.
cases.exclusion: Missing head proof and dismissed reviews cannot contribute a counted round.

cases.name: hydrated review clocks require a complete consistent reviewer cohort
cases.inclusion: An earlier submitted review establishes the current reviewer participation clock.
cases.exclusion: Duplicate, malformed and missing-current cohort members withhold participation and round facts; a later submission cannot move the first clock into a new window.

cases.name: raw feedback and independently accepted feedback remain separate
cases.inclusion: Two distinct submitted review objects yield two raw feedback groups; an independently authorized synthetic receipt qualifies its exact target.
cases.exclusion: Replaying one review, pending reviews, raw-only evidence, self-acceptance and rejected receipts do not create extra accepted feedback.

cases.name: a resolver transition requires its own actor and time
cases.inclusion: A host-proven timestamped resolution attributes its observed unit to the transition actor.
cases.exclusion: Current resolvedBy, missing event time and author-role selection cannot supply a period resolution.

cases.name: duration samples retain readiness cohorts, censoring and unknown clocks
cases.inclusion: One proven two-hour pair yields one sample, median2 and p75=2 while a second PR is censored.
cases.exclusion: Missing readiness is separately counted, no complete pair remains unavailable, a later response cannot move the readiness cohort, and individual ranking is rejected.

cases.name: issue reporting, closing and implementation remain different roles
cases.inclusion: A closed issue retains one reporter unit and a separate closer stewardship unit.
cases.exclusion: An assignee receives neither unit; a closed snapshot does not prove its closer, a missing reporter is not filled from the sender, and closing does not establish resolution or a confirmed bug.

cases.name: label additions require their own collected actor, label identity and exact hydrated revision
cases.inclusion: A collected labeled event carries its own editor, target and timestamp through hydration to one replay-stable candidate unit.
cases.exclusion: Unidentified/unrelated label targets, changed revisions, wrong subjects, missing actors, bots and current labels do not create user contribution.

cases.name: assignment history credits its editor rather than the current assignee
cases.inclusion: An assigned event credits the distinct observed editor, not the issue reporter or current assignee.
cases.exclusion: Missing assignee identity, changed hydrated target, wrong subject, unknown actors, bots and a current assignee list are excluded.

cases.name: collected milestone membership remains distinct from milestone definitions
cases.inclusion: Actual collection and exact hydration preserve the membership actor, target and clock. Add/remove actions remain two raw events; the separate explicit grouping helper marks their one-session reversal without qualified curation.
cases.exclusion: Missing or unrelated milestone targets, changed revisions, current snapshot milestones and milestone-definition events do not produce membership.

cases.name: public pin and lock facets share one actor/item/UTC-day group
cases.inclusion: Four actor-backed public facets and their replay contribute one day group; a separate UTC day contributes a second.
cases.exclusion: Current pin/lock fields, private repositories, organization block actions and personal ranking are excluded.

cases.name: the default hydrated sequence credits earliest eligible nonself reviewers and exact-time ties
cases.inclusion: COMMENTED and CHANGES_REQUESTED reviews at the same earliest eligible time each give their actual author one PR unit; source order and replay cannot break the tie.
cases.exclusion: Earlier self/bot and pending reviews do not win; later, missing or conflicting cohorts and an unproved special action cannot mint first-review participation.

cases.name: a proven title or body text difference credits the edit actor, not the item author
cases.inclusion: One webhook edit whose prior title or body text differs from the current text gives its editor one observed triager unit, once across replays and once when title and body change together.
cases.exclusion: Missing, empty, equal, non-text or unrelated-field edit history, a missing event proof or clock, an unknown or bot editor in the user lens, a private repository, an out-of-window edit and the initial issue representation contribute nothing.

cases.name: a published Project status update credits its publisher and stays separate from neighbouring field subtypes
cases.inclusion: A proven published-update transition with an observed publisher gives one triager unit, once across replays; two publications at different source times give two.
cases.exclusion: No-op or incomplete transitions, a missing event proof, unsupported subtypes, project status, item-field and issue-field changes, an unknown or bot publisher in the user lens, a private repository and an out-of-window publication do not count as project updates.

cases.name: an intentional, publicly verified duplicate mark credits the triage actor once per mark event
cases.inclusion: One duplicate relation event gives its actor one unit; replay and swapped endpoints of that same event stay one canonical unit and a different canonical issue is a second unit. A later removal or un-mark of the same pair is not a reversal today and is recorded as a second raw unit.
cases.exclusion: Automatic relations, unverified public endpoints, other or malformed relation kinds, a missing event proof, an unknown or bot actor in the user lens, a private repository, an out-of-window mark, a plain issue closure and a related-issue link are not duplicate resolution.

cases.name: an accepted finding requires an independent receipt, not issue closure
cases.inclusion: An independently reviewed receipt on the reporter's issue fact gives the reporter one qualified unit on the acceptance clock, once across replays, while the raw issue unit remains.
cases.exclusion: A closed issue, a rejected receipt, a self or unauthorized reviewer, a different actor, a missing target or evidence, an unverified or ineligible receipt, the observed lens and out-of-window acceptance do not count.

cases.name: an accepted issue resolution credits the reviewed deliverable author, not the closer or assignee
cases.inclusion: An independently reviewed receipt on the merged deliverable fact gives its author one qualified unit on the acceptance clock, once across replays.
cases.exclusion: A closed assigned issue, a rejected receipt, a self or unauthorized reviewer, the closer as a substituted actor, a missing target or evidence, an unverified or ineligible receipt, the observed lens and out-of-window acceptance do not count.

cases.name: an accepted clarification requires an independent receipt on a proven edit
cases.inclusion: An independently reviewed receipt on the editor's proven edit fact gives the editor one qualified unit on the acceptance clock, once across replays, while the raw edit unit remains.
cases.exclusion: A raw edit, unchanged text, a rejected receipt, a self or unauthorized reviewer, the item author as a substituted actor, a missing target or evidence, an unverified or ineligible receipt, the observed lens and out-of-window acceptance do not count.

cases.name: an accepted owner handoff requires an independent receipt, not an assignment notification
cases.inclusion: An independently reviewed receipt on the coordinator's assignment fact gives the coordinator one qualified unit on the acceptance clock, once across replays, while the raw assignment unit remains.
cases.exclusion: A raw assignment, a rejected receipt, a self or unauthorized reviewer, the assignee as a substituted actor, a missing target or evidence, an unverified or ineligible receipt, the observed lens and out-of-window acceptance do not count.

metrics.remaining_scope: Draft/readiness labels and live source approval remain outside this creation-count boundary.
The test assumes an explicitly host-verified readiness cohort; it does not prove timeline collection complete.
Physical default-branch delivery, team fractional shares and transfer conservation remain separate source work.
The fixture supplies synthetic verified links; it does not establish actual people, coauthor verification or fractional physical units.
This establishes actor/lens separation, not the quality of stewardship or a public policy approval.
Reopen-history reconciliation and production cohort completeness remain separate; this suite does not invent either.
The transport is synthetic and does not establish permission or complete real repository history.
These cases cover submitted round grouping and proof, not every eligibility or correction rule.
Standalone inline-comment grouping and substantive review quality are not claimed by these submitted-review cases.
Only the host-proven transition boundary is exercised; real thread identity, reopened histories and feedback-author/fixer attribution require separate evidence.
The engine retains internal actor rows; the public team/repository-only projection and source cohort construction are not certified here.
Public reporter identity is synthetic; source hydration and unboarded selection also have separate existing source-boundary tests.
A closing transition is operational activity, not implementing contribution or accepted resolution.
This tests one observed addition and exact replay. Cross-event reapplication/toggle policy is not certified by a single collected event.
The engine case counts raw events and exact replay. The separate explicit synthetic grouping helper does not approve the organization correction interval or award qualified curation.
The engine case counts raw events and exact replay. The separate explicit synthetic grouping helper does not approve the organization correction interval or award qualified curation.
Issue-comment pin history and unsupported discussion stewardship require their own proven source or reviewed receipt; no sanction, offender or justification is inferred.
The transport is synthetic and complete only within the fixture. It certifies no review substance, reviewer expertise, source authorization or real history completeness.

The normalizer proves a text difference only; it does not assess whether the edit is meaningful, formatting-only or one item-day group. Native edit-history acquisition and live source approval remain separate.
The transition shape is supplied by an enriched synthetic envelope; the optional Project status-update feature, substantive content and native webhook collection are not established.

Preserved unique evidence on the duplicate and an accompanying closure are not verified by the normalizer; only the intentional, publicly verified, event-proven relation and its canonical pair are. The normalizer does not gate on the relationship action: a mark followed by a removal or un-mark of the same pair yields two raw units, so pair uniqueness holds per mark event only and reversal handling is remaining scope.
The receipt gate checks independence and target actor identity only. The substance of the finding, its version selection and collaborator attribution rest on the reviewer and separate source work.
The closing link between the issue and the deliverable and the quality of the solution are not verified by the receipt gate; only the reviewed target actor is credited.
Whether an edit improved scope, reproduction or acceptance criteria is the reviewer's judgment; the gate does not group edits into clarification groups.
The gate does not verify the handoff note, the receiving owner's acceptance or documentation; it credits the reviewed target actor on an independent receipt.

remaining_gap.rule: This value must equal the deferred metric count, and the guard test pins a reviewed literal ceiling it may not exceed. Lower both in the same reviewed change that moves a metric into a semantic case or existing evidence; never raise either to admit a new gap.

deferred.reason: A dedicated admitted source, exact acceptance/consent proof, or derivation is still missing. Existing physical #377/#385 paths are preserved, but related work is not an ownership claim or an implementation of retained/commit-attributed line metrics.

These definitions require further actual source/receipt inclusion and exclusion cases. A raw activity or generic approved author fact does not prove exact suggestion links or consented mentorship/onboarding. Reviewed again and left deferred: accepted_suggestions counts on an integrated_at clock and an exact suggestion link, neither of which any admitted source or receipt supplies (the generic receipt carries only an acceptance clock); mentorship and onboarding need recorded mentor/mentee consent and, for onboarding, a first-contribution milestone linked to a support relationship, while the generic receipt checks only reviewer independence and target identity.
